text.content:
A mortal slave of surpassing beauty and skill at song, said to have moved Saulot himself to tears; some believe he Embraced her out of love, though many @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri} deny it since Saulot had forever forbidden such Embraces to his childer. A sister of Samiel and one of Saulot's favored childer, only she could rouse him after the slaughter of the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} Wars, in which he forbade her to take part, and she alone tended him during his trances.

What survives of her music is fragmentary but shows remarkable beauty and complexity; the discovery of any of her songs is cause for celebration among the clan. When Saulot entered his final torpor, Rayzeel vanished altogether, fueling endless speculation that she joined him in torpor or met her destruction. Persistent (if unverified) reports of buskers singing music bearing a striking resemblance to her surviving work suggest she, or her legacy, may yet endure.

Two @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri} — a warrior and a healer — whose fates have been bound together for decades, "as twin lanterns set before a doorway." Yael was born to nomads who tended horses on the Russian steppes; she learned the bow and, unusually early for a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}, took up the crusade against the infernal, journeying into dangerous places to root out servants of Evil. Matthias, a weaver's son who took holy orders at a Benedictine monastery, became renowned as a healer before their paths crossed when Yael sought treatment from him.

Since then, Matthias has served as Yael's chronicler and advisor as well as her constant companion, and rumors of impropriety between them occasionally circulate. Their combined efforts have so far focused on rooting out @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} and Setite influence within the Church, though some believe it only a matter of time before Yael turns her hunt toward @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} havens as well.

Perhaps the greatest warrior yet remaining to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}. Legend holds that he who became Nuriel was a mortal warrior dedicated to Mithras who caught his sire's eye by fighting the sire to a standstill and showing great mettle; his conversion and Embrace has become the stuff of legend among younger @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}, many of whom aspire to become "the next Nuriel."

Many among the warrior caste hope Nuriel might assume a mantle of command like the one Samiel once bore, though Nuriel himself gives the notion little credence. He is regarded as one of the brightest lights remaining to his beleaguered clan.

A crafty English rogue who has made quite a name for himself among the libraries of the Kindred world, stealing precious @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}-related manuscripts and treasures back from the caches of those who claimed them — particularly @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} Magisters, who are his favorite targets and who have placed a substantial (and ever-increasing) bounty on his head. Each increase in the reward seems only to spur him to greater feats of daring.

How Jack-o-Daws came to the Blood is unknown; he refuses to speak of his history, claiming he wishes to spare his sire the embarrassment of being associated with him. Despite this, he is said to remain fiercely loyal to his blood and serves it in his own singular way.

A figure who rivals @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} himself as the most hated name among the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri}: reputedly the one who betrayed the coterie of warriors that ventured into the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali}'s den, and who survived the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} Wars to continue advancing the infernal cause afterward. Some whisper that it was through Ahab's intervention that @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} was able to diablerize Saulot at all, and no atrocity within the clan's history goes unattached to his name.

In the oldest tellings he was nameless, called simply "the Traitor," but storytellers have recently gifted him with the name Ahab. He remains a constant thorn in the clan's side, the bogeyman with which @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.Ei698TPekL0hRbUS]{Salubri} elders frighten their childer, and it is widely believed there will be no peace for the clan until he is run to ground by warrior or avenging angel alike.

pages.name: The Tablet of the Well (Appendix Two)

text.content:
A disputed account recorded by the librarian Simon Ben-Yaakov, concerning a weathered tablet, carved in the style of ancient Sumer, that came into his possession by unknown hands roughly a decade before his writing. The tablet recounts a familiar tale — repeated to Ben-Yaakov over centuries by Cainites who fought the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} at Thera or elsewhere, and even once by a dying @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali} — of how the last three survivors of a blasphemous demon-worshipping tribe were cast into the well where they had thrown their own victims, only to be drained nearly to death and given back just enough vitae by a mysterious Cainite stranger to survive, feed upon the corruption pooling around them, and eventually climb out to trouble the world as the first @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.522046f606404b2b]{Baali}.

In every prior telling, the identity of the stranger who created the Baali went unnamed; the only clue Ben-Yaakov ever heard was a Baali's claim that the stranger came "from where the sky had begun to lighten in anticipation of dawn." The tablet, however, names the stranger outright: Saulot. Ben-Yaakov professed his intent to destroy the tablet and this record of it, dismissing it as a @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere} fabrication meant to discredit Saulot's legacy — though he closes by admitting he may not have that luxury.
